observations: All three source objects remain complete within their panels: one closed rack appliance, one layered SSD with repeated chip-detail views, one virtual-open HDD.

SSD top cover, PCB, base shell, screws and left repeated package details retain adopted form; source detail repetitions do not create additional SSDs.
HDD visibly separates disk/spindle and arm/actuator geometry; one visible disk surface does not establish hidden platter or head counts.
All five leader endpoints are on their intended source objects and remain visible as blue dots.
01 reaches a front tray; 02 reaches the SSD main PCB/package area; 03 reaches the upper-left repeated chip package; 04 reaches the HDD spindle's visible face; 05 reaches the arm crossing the disk.
04 is labeled whole HDD virtual opening, so its spindle-face point is not falsely certified as a bare platter anchor. 05 wording covers disk/arm structural relationship.
All headings, explanations and lower access options are legible at native size. No text/leader crossing, overlapping headings, truncated footnotes, edge cut-offs or missing source structure found.
The local and network read/write strips are separate alternatives. No arrow serializes system→SSD→HDD; no protocol or RAID claim is made from outer shape.
Eight trays, source chip-detail repeats, unknown HDD internal count and campus 0 storage entities are explicitly bounded in figure text.
